mood.p: Zondag wordt volgens Weeronline een zonnige en droge dag: een zwakke tot matige zuidoostenwind trekt warmere lucht aan en het wordt overal boven de 20 graden, in het zuiden 23 tot 24 graden en plaatselijk zelfs 25. Na het weekend gaat het nog verder omhoog, met dinsdag in het zuidoosten mogelijk rond de 29 graden, uitzonderlijk warm voor eind september. Die nazomer staat in contrast met de droogte: op de IJssel geldt eenrichtingsverkeer voor schepen omdat het water te laag staat. In Den Haag draait alles om de begroting, nu Pro en Volt samen optrekken om het minderheidskabinet-Jetten extra toezeggingen af te dwingen. Aan de pomp voelt iedereen de oorlog in het Midden-Oosten, met benzine op een recordprijs van 2,727 euro per liter. Amsterdam is nog aangeslagen door de dodelijke schietpartij op een vol terras bij de NDSM-werf.

global.h3: Trump rejects Iran's seven-day plan to reopen Hormuz
global.summary: On Saturday 26 September Trump dismissed an Iranian roadmap to reopen the Strait of Hormuz within a week, while Tehran said it will not drop its conditions.
body: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi unveiled the proposal at the UN General Assembly on Friday. It asks Washington to lift its naval blockade of Iranian ports, release frozen Iranian funds and restore the waiver on oil sanctions, after which the strait would reopen and talks on a final deal would start by day seven.

Speaking at the White House, Trump said Iran only wanted a deal because it was losing badly and called the offer unacceptable. The Wall Street Journal reported that he has told aides he expects to resume bombing Iran after the November midterms, and he posted a map renaming the waterway the 'Trump Strait'.

Araghchi said Iran was still waiting for a formal answer through mediators and that any reopening depends on its conditions being met. Tehran also wants a ceasefire on all fronts, which would require Israel to halt strikes on Hezbollah in Lebanon.

global.h3: Russia and Ukraine trade strikes, at least 10 dead
global.summary: Overnight attacks into Saturday 26 September killed four people in Ukraine and six in Russia and occupied areas, officials on both sides said.
body: In Zaporizhzhia two women died under the rubble of their home after a Russian barrage of drones and missiles, and a separate strike killed two people in Sumy. President Zelenskyy said Russia was escalating daily and urged partners to respond more forcefully.

Ukrainian drones killed three people in Russia's Krasnodar region and set fire to two industrial sites, reportedly including an oil refinery. The Moscow-installed head of occupied Zaporizhzhia said three more people died there. The violence comes as the US pushes for talks and Moscow accuses Europe of blocking them.

global.h3: Danish intelligence: Russia could strike NATO within months
global.summary: Denmark's military intelligence service warned on 24 September of a 'low but growing risk' of a limited Russian attack on a NATO member.
body: The Danish Defence Intelligence Service said Moscow appears more willing to take risks after four and a half years of war. A limited strike with long-range weapons on infrastructure that supports Ukraine could come in the coming months, aimed at diverting European resources and splitting the alliance.

The agency saw no signs of a full invasion but said Russia might send small numbers of troops without insignia into bordering NATO states. The same day Poland called a fire at a Starlink ground station an act of sabotage.

global.h3: Drone incursions push Europe's east toward open confrontation
global.summary: Moldova recorded four Russian drones in its airspace this week, two of which exploded on its territory, as neighbours call the attacks deliberate.
body: DW reports that drone overflights have become almost daily in parts of central and southeastern Europe since the summer, forcing airspace closures and airport suspensions. Poland, Romania and Moldova are now regularly hit by spillover from Russian strikes on Ukraine.

Officials in the Baltic states, Poland, Romania and Moldova increasingly describe the incidents as intentional aggression rather than hybrid warfare. Analysts expect Moscow to intensify sabotage and airspace violations in the months ahead.

global.h3: Saudi Arabia intercepts six Houthi missiles aimed at oil route
global.summary: The Saudi-led coalition said Houthi missiles targeted Taif and the Red Sea port area of Yanbu, pushing oil to a one-week high.
body: Yanbu is the kingdom's main alternative export route while the Strait of Hormuz is disrupted, and its east-west pipeline is only now restarting after drone strikes earlier this month. The Houthis said they were aiming at Riyadh and Saudi Aramco facilities.

Oil rose about 3% before easing on reports of US-Iran contacts over Hormuz. The Houthis declared a naval blockade of Saudi Arabia in July and recently seized Yemen's entire western coast, reaching the Bab el-Mandeb strait.

global.h3: Pakistan and Afghanistan clash again on the border
global.summary: Pakistani sources said several Afghan Taliban fighters were killed in cross-border fire in the Gulistan area on Friday 25 September.
body: The clashes followed Pakistani air strikes on 10 locations in Afghanistan's Kandahar, Paktia and Khost provinces on Thursday. Islamabad said it was responding to a drone incursion, which the Taliban government denies, and Kabul promised an appropriate response.

The escalation threatens mediation by China, Turkiye, Qatar and Saudi Arabia after the neighbours' worst fighting in years in February. Pakistan accuses Kabul of sheltering militants, a charge the Taliban reject.

global.h3: Fighting in Tigray raises fears of a new Ethiopian war
global.summary: Clashes between Tigrayan forces and the federal army have spread into Afar and Amhara, with internet and phone services disrupted.
body: Residents report panic buying and cannot reach their money through digital apps, as ATMs in the region stopped working months ago. Relations between Addis Ababa and the TPLF have worsened for more than six months.

Each side blames the other: the TPLF says it is resisting a federal offensive with drone strikes, while the government says Tigrayan forces struck first after seizing airports. The fighting puts the 2022 Pretoria peace deal under severe strain.

global.h3: Sudan's army takes Sodari as RSF drones hit El Obeid
global.summary: The army and allied Joint Force captured the North Kordofan town of Sodari on 25 September, while an RSF drone strike on a displacement shelter in El Obeid killed two.
body: The capture extends the military's westward push after it took towns on the El Obeid to Khartoum road in July, though the RSF still holds positions west and south of El Obeid. Local sources alleged that around 17 prisoners were killed when troops entered Sodari.

Saudi Arabia filed a complaint at the UN Security Council accusing the RSF of a drone strike on a King Salman relief truck near El Obeid. The RSF has stepped up drone attacks on frontline cities in recent weeks.

global.h3: Trump-Xi summit heavy on pageantry, light on results
global.summary: Xi Jinping's first Washington visit in over a decade ended with a trade truce extended to 10 January and plans for two more meetings.
body: The leaders met behind closed doors for about 90 minutes, with no sign of breakthroughs on AI, Taiwan, trade or the Iran war. Senate Democrats and former diplomats criticised the state visit for favouring ceremony over substance.

Xi again raised the 'Thucydides Trap' and argued the risk of conflict between rising and established powers can be overcome. The FT reports the two will meet twice more after the summit left core tensions unresolved.

global.h3: German and Russian foreign ministers meet for first time since 2022
global.summary: Johann Wadephul and Sergei Lavrov held a 20-minute meeting at the UN on Saturday 26 September, requested by Berlin.
body: Wadephul said he urged Moscow to step back from its dangerous escalation toward Germany, Europe and NATO, raised drone incursions and pressed for a Black Sea grain export arrangement. The talks ended with a handshake.

Lavrov said nothing new came out of the conversation. In his General Assembly speech he defended the war in Ukraine, vowed Russia would see it through and accused Europe of trying to derail peace talks.

global.h3: Pope Leo draws 800,000 to Paris after warning on AI
global.summary: The Vatican estimated 800,000 people attended Pope Leo XIV's open-air Mass on Place de la Concorde on Saturday 26 September.
body: The turnout was about 200,000 more than had registered, with crowds lining the Champs-Elysees as the American pope passed in the popemobile. It was the high point of his first visit to France as pope.
Earlier in the trip he gave a major speech on artificial intelligence and Europe's future, warning against a 'paradise of machines' and insisting technology must stay at the service of people.

global.h3: United Russia wins record 349 Duma seats
global.summary: Final results published on 25 September gave the Kremlin party 349 of 450 seats in Russia's first wartime parliamentary vote.
body: United Russia took 58% of the party-list vote and 209 single-seat districts, beating its 2016 record of 343 seats. The Communists came second with 37 seats, followed by LDPR, New People and A Just Russia.

Turnout in the 18 to 20 September vote was put at 59.8%. Independent observers called it the least competitive election in modern Russian history, and the new Duma will include 46 veterans of the war in Ukraine.

global.summary: Provisional results give the Authenticity and Modernity Party 97 of 395 seats, with turnout down to 38%.
body: PAM overtook its senior coalition partner RNI, which won 66 seats, while Istiqlal took 65 and the Islamist PJD rebounded from 13 to 54. The king appoints the prime minister from the largest party, putting PAM in line to lead a new coalition.

It was the first vote since the Gen Z protests of last year, and the next government faces pressure on jobs, wages and living costs. It will also manage heavy investment ahead of Morocco co-hosting the 2030 World Cup.

global.h3: Polls point to a punishing midterm for Republicans
global.summary: With the 3 November midterms weeks away, a CNN poll has Trump 34 points underwater, far worse than before the GOP's 2006 and 2018 losses.
body: CNN's poll of polls puts Trump 29 points net negative, against roughly 13 to 15 points at the same stage in 2018. Analysts say he appears to be the most unpopular president on the eve of a midterm in modern polling.
An Emerson survey gives Democrats an 11-point lead on the generic congressional ballot. Democrats need a net gain of four seats to win the Senate, where Republicans hold 53 seats.

global.h3: Six dead, four of them US tourists, in Athens building blast
global.summary: A suspected gas explosion brought down a two-storey building in Athens' historic Plaka district on Friday 25 September.
body: Rescuers recovered six bodies, including four people believed to be American tourists and an elderly British-Greek couple who lived upstairs. Two women were hurt in an adjacent building, and neighbouring properties were evacuated.

Athens mayor Haris Doukas blamed a major gas leak and said two badly damaged buildings may have to be demolished. Local residents had earlier warned authorities and network operators about risks, and officials now face questions over the response.

global.h3: UN: Gaza suffers worst economic collapse on record
global.summary: An UNCTAD report released on 24 September found 90% of working-age Gazans jobless and per capita GDP at $0.58 a day in 2025.
body: The agency estimates 92% of Gaza's business premises have been damaged or destroyed, and industrial and farm output is down 94%. Daily income per person is 82% below the already low 2022 level, leaving the population wholly dependent on food aid.
UNCTAD's acting chief said the collapse has wiped out decades of development. The report describes the strip's economy as the most severe crisis it has ever recorded.

global.h3: Israel to let EU-funded water projects into Gaza
global.summary: Israel pledged to admit 43 million euros of EU aid for essential services such as water pumps, the first such projects in a year.
body: EU Commissioner Dubravka Suica secured the promise from Israeli Foreign Minister Gideon Saar on the margins of the UN General Assembly. The project aims to cut Gazans' exposure to sewage and disease from waste piling up in the streets.

Separately the UK announced an 88 million pound package for Gaza and the West Bank, including emergency water trucking for 150,000 people. The US-led Board of Peace has set out a six-month plan needing 2.45 billion dollars for its first 66 projects.

global.h3: Nepal PM calls deadly glacier flood a warning to the world
global.summary: Balendra Shah told the UN that the 26 August disaster, which killed at least 1,453 people, demands faster climate action.
body: The torrent of mud, rock and water was triggered by a glacial collapse near the China-Tibet border. Nepal's disaster authority says 5,500 people remain missing and 13,795 were rescued.

World Weather Attribution described the event as a compound crisis driven by long-term warming, glacier retreat, permafrost thaw and unstable geology. Shah noted Nepal produces under 0.1% of global emissions yet pays a colossal price.

global.h3: Nor'easter floods US north-east, 100,000 lose power
global.summary: A slow-moving storm battered New Jersey, New York, Delaware and Massachusetts on Saturday 26 September with high winds and coastal flooding.
body: Tens of millions of people were in the storm's path, and forecasters warned of more wind, high tides and heavy rain over several days. On Long Island some residents paddled kayaks down flooded streets.

Events were cancelled from Massachusetts to Maryland ahead of the storm, which was forecast to bring gusts up to 60 mph. Marina owners on the Jersey Shore reported water levels not seen since Hurricane Sandy.

netherlands.h3: Pro and Volt join forces to force budget deal
netherlands.summary: On Saturday 26 September Pro and Volt began joint budget talks with PM Jetten, offering the minority cabinet a stable majority in both chambers.
body: Pro leader Jesse Klaver said the combined votes of his left-wing party and pro-European Volt would carry the D66, VVD and CDA cabinet through both houses. In the Senate, Pro is the largest group but still needs Volt's two seats to reach the 16 the coalition lacks.

Jetten says ministers have prepared a new offer on welfare, purchasing power and the Box 3 asset tax. Finance minister Eelco Heinen has already postponed or scrapped about half of the 6 billion euros in welfare cuts, but Pro wants more.

The VVD fears that concessions to the left will push its voters to JA21 and the PVV. JA21 argues for deeper welfare cuts and lower taxes, while Klaver has threatened to block the whole budget if the cabinet tries separate deals per ministry.

netherlands.h3: Cabinet tables new Box 3 offer to win budget support
netherlands.summary: After Friday's council of ministers on 25 September, Jetten said a revised package on purchasing power, social security and Box 3 is on the table.
body: The coalition parties had long been split on the wealth tax, with D66 and CDA on one side and the VVD on the other. Jetten said they now see room for a good proposal but gave no details or funding plan, although the changes are expected to cost billions.

Heinen's draft budget had proposed higher taxes on labour to fill the gap, while many MPs want the money raised from wealth instead. Jetten also dropped his refusal to talk to the BBB, which had backed a no-confidence motion against the cabinet.

netherlands.h3: Jetten tells UN: hands off the ICC
netherlands.summary: In his first UN General Assembly speech on Thursday 24 September, PM Rob Jetten defended the International Criminal Court in The Hague.
body: Without naming Donald Trump, Jetten said attempts to undermine the court threaten the entire international legal order. The US has already sanctioned 13 ICC staff, including its president, and is reported to be weighing sanctions on the court as a whole.
As host state, the Netherlands must help the court with security, visas and transport of defendants and witnesses. Jetten also called for Russia to be held to account for its war in Ukraine.

netherlands.h3: Justice minister Van Weel survives no-confidence vote
netherlands.summary: David van Weel apologised to MPs on 24 September over his account of about 10,000 criminal complaints police left uninvestigated.
body: In June he told parliament that most of the cases were reports rather than formal complaints. The Court of Audit later found only 10% were verbal reports, and said victims of serious crimes such as sexual offences had been denied justice.

Van Weel first called the dispute a difference of insight, which angered MPs. He later admitted he had given the impression of trivialising the report, and a PVV motion of no confidence failed to pass.

netherlands.h3: State orders inquiry into decades of donor conception abuses
netherlands.summary: The health ministry has commissioned an independent historical review of sperm donation, funded with 650,000 euros.
body: The probe follows revelations that a prolific donor kept donating for years despite being known to authorities. Health minister Sophie Hermans said no full review has been done before, and it will cover the period from the 1950s to the 2025 law capping donors at 12 mothers.

ZonMw will oversee the research, which should begin around mid-2027 and report before the 2030 evaluation of the donor law. The role of the health inspectorate and the ministry itself will also be examined.

netherlands.h3: Petrol hits record 2.727 euros per litre
netherlands.summary: The recommended pump price for petrol rose 1.5 cents to a record 2.727 euros on Friday 25 September, UnitedConsumers data show.
body: Petrol was almost 50 cents cheaper before the Middle East war began. Diesel eased slightly to 2.794 euros, though the EU average diesel price hit a record on Thursday.

A possible US ban on diesel exports could push prices higher, with Morgan Stanley warning Europe would be hit hardest. Dutch stations near the border also fear losing customers to Germany, which is cutting fuel prices by 17 cents a litre.

netherlands.h3: Cabinet wants energy firms to fund gas storage
netherlands.summary: With state operator EBN facing a loss of about 1 billion euros, the government wants suppliers such as Essent, Eneco and Vattenfall to hold their own reserves.
body: Storage at Norg, Grijpskerk, Bergermeer and Alkmaar is currently filled at public expense, but high prices give companies no incentive to stock up. The Netherlands cut its November filling target from 74% to 64%, and storage stands at 57.5%.
Since Groningen production ended, the sites are filled with imported gas, much of it costly LNG from the US. A similar storage obligation already applies in Austria.

netherlands.summary: CBS figures show prices rose 3.3% year on year in August while dipping 0.1% from July. Transactions fell 2.9%.
body: Annual growth peaked at 11.5% in January 2025 and has cooled steadily since. The average price of an existing home rose to 503,523 euros after passing half a million in July.
Prices are now 17.8% above the previous peak of July 2022.

netherlands.h3: Experts: mid-market rentals key to unlocking housing
netherlands.summary: Housing experts say the cabinet's new acceleration plan will not end stagnation unless it adds mid-market rental homes.
body: Housing minister Elanor Boekholt-O'Sullivan presented an action plan this week focused on building faster. Vastgoed Belang calculates that 76,000 mid-market rentals have left the market since the Affordable Rent Act took effect.

Pararius founder Jasper de Groot said the cabinet is partly reversing its own earlier measures. VU economist Hans Koster noted that tenants in cheap social housing have little incentive to move even when their incomes rise.

netherlands.h3: Tata Steel deal deadline pushed to March 2027
netherlands.summary: The cabinet, Tata Steel and Noord-Holland extended talks on a tailored green deal, worth up to 2 billion euros in state aid, to 1 March 2027.
body: Climate minister Stientje van Veldhoven said the main cause is a regional agency's plan to revoke permits for the IJmuiden coke plants, which would change the timeline and costs. The cabinet chose not to walk away despite the criminal pollution case brought against the company in July.
Frisse Wind and Greenpeace welcomed the pause, calling for independent health measurements before any deal. Van Veldhoven said the 2 billion euro ceiling will not be raised.

netherlands.h3: Drought forces one-way shipping on the IJssel
netherlands.summary: Since Friday 25 September barges from Arnhem to Zutphen must detour up to 300 km because the river is too shallow for ships to pass.
body: Rijkswaterstaat says the summer drought has cut Rhine flow at Lobith to about 600 cubic metres per second. Inland shipping group KBN said boats were already sailing with half or a third of their normal loads.
The detour will add further costs for a sector already hit by low water limits.

netherlands.h3: Prison officer shot dead on busy Amsterdam terrace
netherlands.summary: Marcel Blijd, a warden at Zaanstad prison, was shot at close range at the NDSM quay on Friday afternoon 25 September.
body: Witnesses said the gunman argued with Blijd about a loose dog before firing, then threw the gun into the water and waited for police. Dozens of people on the terrace saw the attack, and the suspect is in custody.

Het Parool reported that the suspect was previously held at Zaanstad, which houses some of Amsterdam's most dangerous offenders. Detectives are investigating a possible link to Blijd's 30-year prison career.

netherlands.h3: Stress-related sick days up 12% in a year
netherlands.summary: Occupational health services ArboNed and HumanCapitalCare report stress absence rose 12% in a year and 49% since 2021.
body: Workload, money worries, health issues and caring for relatives are the main drivers. Average absenteeism was 4.9% from July 2025 to June 2026, up from 4.8% a year earlier.
Only 11% of absence reports account for 83% of all sick days. ArboNed's medical director urged employers to spot warning signs before staff drop out long term.
